sections.html:
Two offices handle your bill. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) decides what the property is worth, and the Sheriff collects the money. McCreary County has no incorporated city, so there is no city tax office and no city levy. County government is the only local government covering every resident, and school and district levies fill out the rest of the bill.

The PVA's mailing address is PO Box 609, Whitley City, KY 42653, phone (606) 376-2514, fax (606) 376-4152. The Sheriff is at (606) 376-2322. The County Clerk, who files deeds and takes over any unpaid bill, is at (606) 376-2411. The fiscal court meets at 1 North Main Street in Whitley City on the second Thursday evening of the month, starting at six.

Kentucky law (KRS 134.015) values property as of January 1 and expects the bill paid before the year ends. The Sheriff takes payment through April 15, and the cost climbs in steps.

What a McCreary County bill costs by payment date
When you payWhat changes
By November 12 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount on the bill
January5 percent added
After January10 percent added

If the bill is still unpaid after April 15, it moves to the County Clerk. Two warning letters from the county attorney follow, and a sale of the tax certificate can come three to four and a half months after the transfer. Whoever buys the certificate may add charges, so pay the Sheriff before that point.

sections.h2: What a McCreary County house costs in tax
sections.html:
Bills here are low by Kentucky standards because home values are low. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $85,300, and the state's 2025 rate is 10.6 cents on every $100 of assessed value. The county, the school board and special districts add their own levies on top. The PVA can add them up for any one address.

About 74.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, and typical rent is $577 a month. New construction was nil in 2025, with 0 permits, so the market is almost entirely existing houses. The population was 17,124 in 2025, and the 2020 count showed 6,892 housing units, roughly one in eight of them empty.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption for seniors and disabled owners
sections.html:
Anyone in McCreary County who qualifies can use the statewide homestead deduction. Owners who have turned 65, or who count as totally disabled, see $49,100 dropped from assessed value for 2025 and 2026, and that happens before rates are applied. On a house near the $85,300 median, that removes a large share of the taxable value.

Apply in person at the PVA office in Whitley City. Bring a birth certificate, driver's license or passport as proof of age. A claim based on disability needs a government or retirement-plan finding of total disability and has to be renewed every year. Owners with a service-connected disability rating, and anyone already ruled totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems, don't have to renew.

Your first move is a conference with the PVA or a deputy. An appeal from someone who skipped it is turned away, and staff must walk you through how your number was built. Then:

  • Look over the roll during the 13 days that start after the first Monday in May.
  • File your appeal with the County Clerk by the first working day after the roll closes.
  • Attach evidence about land and buildings: insurance records, construction costs, comparable sales and photographs. A survey helps with rural tracts. Appeals with no support tend to fail.
  • Attend the local board of property owners when it meets, about a month after the roll closes. It takes evidence only when both sides are present.

Skip the hearing and you lose the next stage, the Kentucky Claims Commission. If bills have already gone out and the board sets a value above what you claimed, a supplemental bill covers the difference.

Unpaid tax stays with the house. Under Kentucky law it is the owner's personal debt from January 1, and a lien under KRS 134.420 can last 11 years no matter whose name is on the deed. Once the bill reaches the Clerk, interest of 1 percent a month starts, plus commissions for the Clerk and county attorney and a recording fee.

The title company will ask for a payoff figure before it releases sale money. The Sheriff provides it through April 15, and the Clerk provides it after that. Order it early, because the sale price has to cover the payoff before the seller sees anything.

A cash sale as-is can help an heir or an owner who is behind: no repair bills, no showings, and a closing date you can plan around the payoff. The tax still comes out of the proceeds either way.

sections.h2: Selling a house in McCreary County
sections.html:
McCreary is Kentucky's newest county, formed in 1912 from parts of Pulaski, Wayne and Whitley, and none of it lies inside an incorporated city. Whitley City is the seat, with Pine Knot and Stearns as the other named communities. Federal land covers much of the map: the Daniel Boone National Forest holds roughly 43 percent and the Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area roughly 18 percent, so private land is limited.

Population peaked at 18,306 in 2010 and fell 7.7 percent to 16,888 by 2020, then rose 1.4 percent to the 2025 figure. About 17.9 percent of residents are 65 or older. Prices sit near the county's low median home value, so price carefully and expect buyers to compare against nearby rentals.

A sale here goes in a predictable order. Ask the Sheriff or Clerk for the tax payoff. Confirm with the PVA whether a homestead claim is on the parcel, since removing or changing it affects the next bill. Gather the deed and any lien paperwork, then hand the payoff to the closing agent so the tax is paid out of proceeds. The County Clerk records the new deed once the sale closes.

If the house came through an estate, expect the deed work to take longer, and bring the paperwork showing who has authority to sell.

Before you list, walk the parcel with the PVA's records in hand. Check that the acreage, the building description and the owner name all match what you plan to sell. A wrong acreage figure on the roll is easy to fix with the PVA staff before a buyer's lender spots it. Rural tracts in this county are the usual place for mismatches, and a recent survey settles most questions.

faqs.q: Is there a city property tax in McCreary County?
faqs.a: No. The county has no incorporated city, so there is no city levy. School and district levies still appear on the bill.

faqs.q: Who do I pay for McCreary County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Sheriff at (606) 376-2322 any time through April 15. The PVA at (606) 376-2514 sets values and takes exemption papers, never payments.

faqs.q: What is the state rate for 2025?
faqs.a: The state rate is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value for 2025. County, school and district levies add to it.

faqs.q: Can a 65-year-old lower the taxable value?
faqs.a: Yes. Bring proof of age to the PVA office in Whitley City, and $49,100 comes off assessed value for 2025 and 2026 under the homestead deduction.

faqs.q: What happens if my bill moves to the County Clerk?
faqs.a: A lien is recorded and interest runs at 1 percent a month. The certificate may be sold to an investor three to four and a half months after the move.
